Each point on the line averages the weigh-ins from that day and the 13 days before it. Days without a weigh-in are skipped. Each change compares today’s average with the one 7, 30 or 90 days earlier, or with your first weigh-in for all time.

Monthly summary

    Your monthly summary will appear here after your first weigh-in.

    Each month starts with the 14-day average as it began and ends with the average on its last day, so it picks up where the month before ended. When the log starts partway through a month, or has a break of more than two weeks, a date shows which day an average comes from. The weekly trend is as it stood on the month’s last day, and milestones show in the month your average first reached them.

    Body fat

    DateWaist14-day average14-day avg.Body fatEdit measurement

    An estimate from the U.S. Army’s one-site tape formula, using your waist at the navel and your 14-day average on the day you measured. A tape estimate can be several points off a lab scan, so it’s most useful for following your own trend.

    Your data

    Download

    Your weigh-ins as a spreadsheet, with each one’s note and 14-day average. Or everything in your log as JSON: weigh-ins and notes, waist measurements, height, the body fat formula, your goal, units and reminder time.

    Body fat—

    Male: −26.97 − 0.12 × weight (lb) + 1.99 × waist (in). Female: −9.15 − 0.015 × weight (lb) + 1.27 × waist (in). About the formula

    Delete your data?

    This permanently deletes everything in your log, on every device:

    • Your weigh-ins and their notes
    • Your waist measurements and the body fat formula you chose
    • Your goal and your height
    • Your units, which go back to kg and cm
    • Your reminders, which stop on every device
